interpretations: Funding sources are "bigger than average" by number of linked spatial scan records (row count per source). The average is taken across funding sources, and the output is one row
Size is the sum of `boxy` per funding source. Sources whose summed `boxy` exceeds the mean of those sums qualify
Size is the sum of `boxz` per funding source
Size is the sum of the per-record `boxy`/`boxz` ratios per funding source
Size is the average `boxy`/`boxz` ratio per funding source. The ratio is both the measure and the size, and sources above the mean of those averages qualify
Size is the number of distinct projects per funding source
Size is the number of distinct `scanspatial` records, counted after the join
Size is the sum of `volm3` per funding source
Size is the sum of `aream2` per funding source
Size is the average bounding box volume (`boxx`×`boxy`×`boxz`) per funding source
The average ratio per source is the mean of the per-record ratios (`AVG(boxy/boxz)`), ignoring records where either value is null
The average ratio per source is the ratio of averages (`AVG(boxy)`/`AVG(boxz)`)
The average ratio per source is the ratio of sums (`SUM(boxy)`/`SUM(boxz)`)
"Ignoring missing values" excludes records where `boxy` or `boxz` is null. Records where `boxz` is zero are also excluded, to avoid division by zero
"Ignoring missing values" excludes only null `boxz`, and zero is treated as a valid value that causes a division error or null
Null `fundflux` is its own group, shown as NULL
Null `fundflux` is its own group, labeled with a placeholder such as 'Unknown' or 'Missing'. Empty strings are merged into it
The size measure is computed over all records in a group. The ratio average ignores nulls
The size measure is computed only over records with non-null `boxy` and `boxz`
The average size threshold is the mean of the per-source sizes, where each source counts equally
The average size threshold is the overall per-record average size across all records, not per source
"Above the average size" means strictly greater than the threshold
"Above the average size" means greater than or equal to the threshold
The final row's "average of their ratios" is the simple mean of the qualifying sources' average ratios
The final row's "average of their ratios" is weighted by record count
The final row's "average of their ratios" is weighted by size
"Their combined size" is the sum of the qualifying sources' sizes
"Their combined size" is the size recomputed over the pooled records of the qualifying sources. For non-additive measures such as distinct counts, this differs from the sum
"How far on average they exceed the average size" is the mean of (source size − threshold) over the qualifying sources
"How far on average they exceed" is the combined size minus the threshold, or that figure divided by the number of qualifying sources
"How far on average they exceed" is expressed as a percentage or ratio above the threshold rather than an absolute difference
"No rounding" means all outputs are returned at full precision
Only projects with at least one linked `scanspatial` record are included (inner join)
Projects without spatial scans are included through a left join. Their size is zero or null, and they may form groups of their own
The join of `scanspatial` to `projects` goes through `arcref`=`arcregistry` only. Operator (`crewref`) links are ignored
The join of `scanspatial` to `projects` also requires the operator to match another table
The ratio is `boxy`/`boxz`, with `boxy` as the numerator
The ratio is cast to float or numeric before dividing, to avoid integer division
Spatial records whose `arcref` has no matching project are excluded
Spatial records whose `arcref` has no matching project are kept as a null funding group
Size is the sum of `boxx` per funding source
Size is the sum of the bounding box volume (`boxx`×`boxy`×`boxz`) per funding source
Size is the average `boxy` per funding source
Size is the average `boxz` per funding source
Size is the average `boxx` per funding source
Size is the average `volm3` per funding source
Size is the average `aream2` per funding source
Size is the number of records per funding source with a non-null, usable `boxy`/`boxz` ratio, meaning the records that enter the ratio average
Size is the number of distinct operators (`crewref`) per funding source
Size is the sum of `groundspan` per funding source
Records where `boxz` is zero are not excluded, and the ratio is turned into NULL with NULLIF so that it is ignored by the average
The final row's "average of their ratios" is the ratio of the qualifying sources' pooled `boxy` and `boxz`, recomputed over their pooled records
"How far on average they exceed the average size" is the average size of the qualifying sources minus the threshold
queries:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT p.fundflux, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM projects p
  JOIN scanspatial s ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS bigger_than_average_sources
FROM c
WHERE n > (SELECT AVG(n) FROM c);

SELECT p.fundflux
FROM projects p
JOIN scanspatial s ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry
GROUP BY p.fundflux
HAVING SUM(s.boxy) > (
  SELECT AVG(t.total)
  FROM (
    SELECT SUM(s2.boxy) AS total
    FROM projects p2
    JOIN scanspatial s2 ON s2.arcref = p2.arcregistry
    GROUP BY p2.fundflux
  ) t
)

SELECT p.fundflux, SUM(s.boxz) AS size
FROM scanspatial s
JOIN projects p ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry
GROUP BY p.fundflux;

SELECT p.fundflux, SUM(s.boxy / s.boxz) AS size
FROM scanspatial s
JOIN projects p ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry
GROUP BY p.fundflux

WITH src AS (
  SELECT p.fundflux AS fundflux, AVG(s.boxy / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio
  FROM scanspatial s
  JOIN projects p ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
)
SELECT fundflux, avg_ratio
FROM src
WHERE avg_ratio > (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM src);
SELECT fundflux, COUNT(DISTINCT arcregistry) AS size FROM projects GROUP BY fundflux
